headline: Going Commando gains Android disc builds and a bundled Windows compiler on develop
summary: Going Commando can now be built from the player's disc on Android, with its remaining assembly compiled on the phone (#300, #310). Windows gains a bundled compiler path too, replacing the need for separately installed build tools (#326). My mods brings gameplay mods, graphics and sound packs, and textures together, while Get mods replaces the built-in browser (#314, #321). These features followed the day's release preparation for launcher 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 (#285, #295).
highlights: Android keeps Going Commando's compiled disc component when its kit is unchanged (#320). Stable-to-Development updates install in place, but returning to Stable still needs a GitHub reinstall (#302).
Mods can provide their own launcher tool pages (#304), and tools show an Always on switch (#329).
Per-game Steam entries and Linux shortcuts landed (#324, closing #318). They have unit tests only and have not been tested on real Steam or Steam Deck.
Drek's Fleet's fighter mission regains its nebula backdrop and missing fleet (#301). HDR becomes Off/On (#308), and freecam's L3+R3 shortcut no longer also opens the map (#330).
Android pad selection opens a game's page before Play, with visible focus from startup (#305, #309, #312). Context-sensitive touch buttons remain an unmerged draft (#319).

Vulkan checks reuse caches and a shared build, and run on pushes (#286, #288, #290, #307). Linux builds shed curl, tar and Steam's libraries (#325). The launcher stops creating an unused home folder (#323).
